cohort: 657 women in Iceland who participated in the Childbirth and Health Cohort Study
finding: A history of violence was associated with poorer self-perceived health, a higher rate of unplanned pregnancies, more cesarean sections, and a perception of worse general health in their child at 18-24 months after birth.
mod_finding: Women with a history of violence were more likely to have deliveries by cesarean section.
